clue.text: Remove a coat — or much more

definitions.text: Remove a coat — or much more

parts.words: Remove a coat — or much more
parts.note: the phrase for taking off one garment is also the phrase for undressing completely, so it covers a coat or everything

explanation.surface: Advice on shedding a single layer, with a cheeky hint at going further.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to take off clothing, whether a single layer or all of it.

clue.text: Arranges parking under cover for games

indicators.note: the parking is covered by the other piece, held inside it

parts.note: sorts means arranges
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone organising covered parking for a sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports are athletic games and competitions.

clue.text: Conditions under which horses race

definitions.meaning: provisos added to a contract or bill
jockeys sit astride the horses, so the horses race beneath them

explanation.surface: A statement about what circumstances apply to horse racing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conditions under which' reads as one phrase about rules; split it after 'Conditions'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added to a document; riders are also those on horseback.

clue.text: New blow follows strike, leading to depression in the land

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a punch is a strike

indicators.note: a new version of the word blow, with letters remade

explanation.surface: A boxing account of one blow after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl-shaped hollow in hills is a landscape feature called by this name.

clue.text: Counterfeiting next year's coins is progressing well

definitions.meaning: faking money in advance, making it before its time

explanation.surface: A forger's early work presented as a success.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means making steady progress, and literally faking ahead of time.

clue.text: Fresh meat sailors swallowed

indicators.note: the meat takes the sailors inside itself, as if eating them

parts.note: veal is calf meat
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A butcher's boast that the new meat was eaten up by the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal means springlike, and spring growth is fresh and new.

clue.text: Demand payment out of turn

parts.note: ex means from or out of
an act is a turn in a variety show

explanation.surface: Asking to be paid at an inappropriate moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of turn' reads as the idiom for speaking at the wrong moment; a turn is a performer's spot in a variety show.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact payment is to demand and enforce it.

clue.text: Recognising gin and tonic ingredients

indicators.note: the letters are components to be mixed, like a drink's contents

explanation.surface: Picking out the components of a familiar cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticing something is recognising or spotting it.

clue.text: Identified boy embracing pretty girl

indicators.note: the boy wraps round the pretty girl, holding her inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a belle is a beautiful girl

explanation.surface: A young man hugging a beautiful girl was recognised.
explanation.definitionFit: Labelled means tagged or identified as something.

clue.text: Commonplace name for a penny-farthing

definitions.meaning: the high-wheeled Victorian bicycle was called by this name to distinguish it from the later safety bicycle

explanation.surface: A remark that the old high-wheeled bicycle had a dull name.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means everyday; the Victorian high-wheeler was known as an 'ordinary' bicycle.

clue.text: Worker goes in taxi from Cambridge

indicators.note: the worker climbs inside the taxi, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: An employee hails a cab and rides away from Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' suggests a labourer, but the crossword convention is the worker ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantab, short for Latin Cantabrigiensis, marks a degree or person belonging to Cambridge University.

clue.text: Soldier-husband who tries to supply all one's needs

definitions.text: who tries to supply all one's needs

parts.note: a general is a high-ranking soldier
to husband resources is to store them up

explanation.surface: A military man whose husbandly role is providing everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' is the verb, to save or conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A village shop selling a wide range of goods aims to meet every need.

clue.text: Light superstructure of the Statue of Liberty

definitions.meaning: a portable lamp or flame held to give light

definitions.text: superstructure of the Statue of Liberty
definitions.meaning: the raised flame held aloft at the top of the New York statue

explanation.surface: A description of the illuminated crown piece of New York's famous statue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held lamp gives light, and the statue raises a flaming one in her right hand.

clue.text: I'd upset a client, just the same

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: an upset overturns things, so the letters of a client are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A professional shrugging that annoying a customer changes nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges A CLIENT into ENTICAL, placed after ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactly alike, matching in every respect, is what just the same means.

clue.text: Yet this could be one word — life

definitions.text: Yet this could be one word
definitions.meaning: a lengthy grammatical sentence, paradoxically a single word when a judge says it

explanation.surface: A paradox: something lengthy that could consist of a single word.
explanation.walkthrough: A judge's single word 'life' passes a lengthy prison term, though a grammatical sentence of one word is hardly lengthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A life term in prison is the classic lengthy custodial penalty handed down by a judge.

clue.text: Skinny artist who has designs on his clients

definitions.text: Skinny artist who has designs on his clients

parts.words: Skinny artist who has designs on his clients
parts.note: an artist working on skin, putting pictures onto customers' bodies

explanation.surface: A thin, scheming painter plotting against customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinny' suggests thin, 'has designs on' suggests scheming; both are literal here.
explanation.definitionFit: This person inks designs onto the skin of customers.

clue.text: Need to have a match around when it's dark

indicators.note: the match is placed round the need

parts.note: a bout is a sporting match
lack means need

explanation.surface: A night fixture requires floodlights.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a period of darkness, with lights out or covered.

clue.text: Quick diet a man ordered

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A man's prescribed diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in the old sense means alive, and animated means lively.

clue.text: Rosalyn and Ethel may be looking for happy relationships

indicators.note: the two names could become something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two women with old-fashioned names are seeking love.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names people who advertise for romance, so they are seeking partners.

clue.text: Necessitate a note before Latin revision

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A school pupil must revise Latin after music.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve as a necessary consequence.

clue.text: People mending pipes

explanation.surface: Workers who repair pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: The same spelling covers needleworkers and drains.
explanation.definitionFit: Needleworkers who stitch are sewers, and drains carrying waste are sewers too.

clue.text: They're responsible for split sides but firm middles

parts.note: CO, company, is a firm
medians are middle values or middle lines

explanation.surface: A joke about entertainers who cause belly laughs while keeping trim waists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split sides' is laughing hard; 'firm middles' looks like a fitness claim but is the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughing until your sides split is caused by funny entertainers on stage.

clue.text: Settle on the end of a bed spring

indicators.note: only the final letter of bed is used

parts.note: a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Sitting on the edge of a mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live or settle somewhere.

clue.text: Cat required? There are quite a few in the pound

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard of Central Asia goes by this name

definitions.text: There are quite a few in the pound
definitions.meaning: sixteen of these weights make a pound avoirdupois

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a cat is needed at the pound, where there are many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' suggests an animals' compound, fitting 'Cat', but it is the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard is also called this; and it is a weight, sixteen to the pound.

clue.text: Not allowed permit for market

parts.note: in games, a ball not allowed is out
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A trader refused a licence to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a market or shop through which goods are sold.

clue.text: I'm back in present command

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to donate is to present a gift

indicators.note: the letters of I'm are turned round to read the other way

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone back in post declaring they are now in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To dominate is to hold command or control over others.

clue.text: Rather small drunk

definitions.meaning: tiny, teeny, a colloquial word for little

explanation.surface: A person a little the worse for drink.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word both for tiny and for mildly tipsy.

clue.text: Hat-clutching salesmen, crawlers

indicators.note: the salesmen hold the hat inside them, gripped

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen holding their hats are fawning toadies.
explanation.walkthrough: TILE as a hat is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Snakes and lizards crawl; reptiles is also a scornful word for fawning people.
